title: Supreme Court Term to Tackle Climate, Gun and Emergency Cases
summary:
The Supreme Court returns Monday to begin its new term, the yearly period when it hears cases and issues decisions. This term, the justices will consider major questions about climate change, guns and how quickly the court acts on emergency requests.

One case involves climate change. The city and county of Boulder, Colorado, sued energy companies Suncor and Exxon Mobil in 2018. Boulder argues that the companies knew they were contributing to climate change and that this caused harm to the area and its residents. The city is seeking money from the companies. The companies say federal law and the Constitution block these kinds of state lawsuits. Lower courts have ruled that the cases belong in state courts, not federal courts. The Supreme Court will hear arguments on October 5 and decide whether Boulder can sue under state law. Justice Samuel Alito recused himself from the case on September 28, meaning he will not take part.

In December, the court will hear arguments about an Illinois law that bans the possession, sale and transfer of assault weapons, including AR-15s. County residents and gun rights organizations sued in 2021, saying the law violated their constitutional rights. The court will decide whether the Second and 14th Amendments give people the right to possess semiautomatic weapons. One expert, French, said that most places in the United States do not ban AR-15s and that the democratic process has largely worked on gun control. Another expert, Howe, said the case could help the court clarify its Second Amendment rulings, an area he called "still in its relative infancy." According to the Congressional Research Service, the court has remained largely silent on the amendment's scope and meaning for more than 200 years.

The court also spends time on its emergency docket, sometimes called the "shadow docket." These are requests that need a fast decision while a case moves through lower courts. The rulings are usually unsigned and do not include long explanations. In September, the court temporarily blocked President Donald Trump's effort to restrict mail-in voting.

More cases may be added in the coming months. The court could still hear cases about the military's ban on transgender members or Trump's appeal in a defamation case brought by writer E. Jean Carroll. Experts say the court now hears relatively few full cases on the merits, and much of its work happens on the emergency docket, where temporary decisions can still have long-term effects.
why_it_matters: Supreme Court rulings can affect laws and rights for everyone in the country, and the emergency docket shows how quickly some decisions are made.

questions.question: What does it mean that Justice Alito recused himself from the Boulder case?
options: He will write the main opinion
He stepped aside and will not take part
He asked the court to move the date
He will lead the oral arguments
questions.correct_answer: He stepped aside and will not take part

questions.question: What did lower courts rule about the climate cases?
options: That the cases belong in state courts, not federal courts
That only the president can decide cases like these
That the energy companies must pay Boulder money right away
That the cases should be dropped before any trial begins
questions.correct_answer: That the cases belong in state courts, not federal courts

questions.question: What will the Supreme Court decide in the Boulder case?
options: Whether Boulder is allowed to ban oil sales in the city
Whether Boulder can sue the energy companies under state law
Whether Suncor is allowed to merge with Exxon Mobil
Whether Colorado must change its own climate rules
questions.correct_answer: Whether Boulder can sue the energy companies under state law

questions.question: What did the Congressional Research Service say about the Second Amendment?
options: The amendment only applies to certain older kinds of guns
The court has ruled on the amendment in nearly every single term
The amendment was changed by the state of Illinois in 2021
The court has remained largely silent on its scope and meaning for over 200 years
questions.correct_answer: The court has remained largely silent on its scope and meaning for over 200 years

questions.question: How are emergency docket rulings usually described in the article?
options: Made only after months of public hearings
Unsigned and without long explanations
Signed by all nine justices with long reports
Final and impossible to change later

questions.question: What happened in the emergency docket in September?
options: The court approved the Illinois assault weapons ban in full
The court ended the military's ban on transgender members for good
The court decided the whole E. Jean Carroll defamation case
The court temporarily blocked an effort to restrict mail-in voting
questions.correct_answer: The court temporarily blocked an effort to restrict mail-in voting

background_read: The Supreme Court is the highest court in the United States.
The Second Amendment and the 14th Amendment are parts of the U.S. Constitution.
